cover: Israeli fire kills four, including a child
Dam opponents refuse talks until detainees freed

stories.label: World · Life & safety
stories.place: Deir el-Balah, Bureij and Khan Younis, Gaza
stories.head: A child among the dead
bullets: A drone hit a tent west of az-Zawayda at dawn, medics say.
A child was killed by Israeli fire in Bureij camp.
No Israeli military comment was reported.
stories.caption:
Since the October 2025 ceasefire, Gaza's health ministry counts 1,602 people killed. No Israeli military comment on Thursday's deaths was reported.
Source: Al Jazeera

stories.label: The Siang dam
stories.head: No talks while they are held
bullets: A farmers' forum turned down the chief minister's talks offer for 5–7 November.
It wants detainees freed and armed forces withdrawn first.
A foot march from Geku to Itanagar is under way; no government reply was reported.
stories.caption:
Villages along the Siang fear an 11,000 MW dam would submerge their land. Their forum says it will talk only once those detained are freed.
Source: Arunachal Times

stories.label: Protest in Delhi
stories.head: Parents removed from Raj Ghat
bullets: Police detained Ankita Bhandari's parents late Wednesday; her father says they were dragged.
Police cite a prohibitory order and a planned indefinite sit-in.
They say they took her unwell mother to hospital.
stories.caption:
Her father says they were held about two hours without water. Police deny tracking the couple's phones.
Source: ThePrint

stories.label: World · Assembly
stories.head: A day of strikes over pay
bullets: 575,000 marched by the Interior Ministry's count; 1.6 million by the CGT union's.
Police used tear gas in Lyon and at a Paris high school.
The government defended police and said any abuses would be investigated.
stories.caption:
Unions called the day for higher wages. The ministry says 53 officers were injured; no count of injured protesters was reported.
Source: franceinfo

hope_caption:
Two Indian courts stood up for people in custody: the 24-hour clock to see a magistrate starts at detention, and an FIR was ordered against an officer over altered arrest papers.
Source: LiveLaw
